articles.title: The Fascinating Science of How We Think Not with the Brain But with the World
articles.highlight: 当思考越过大脑的边界，我们反而能更专注、更深刻地理解、更富想象地创造——去容纳单靠大脑根本无法设想的想法。
articles.summary: 这篇文章讨论“延展心智”的科学：思考并不只发生在大脑里，也发生在我们使用的笔记本、工具与周遭环境中。它值得一读，因为它提醒我们重新看待“思考发生在哪里”，并解释了为什么借助外部载体能让专注、理解与创造力同时提升。
articles.failureAnalysis: 核心启发：与其一味逼大脑硬扛，不如把外部工具和环境一并设计进思考流程，这往往能带来远超单靠脑力的效果。
articles.sourceExcerpt: "By reaching beyond the brain... we are able to focus more intently, comprehend more deeply, and create more imaginatively — to entertain ideas that would be literally unthinkable by the brain alone."

en.summary: The article explores the science of the extended mind: thinking does not happen only inside the brain, but also through the notebooks, tools, and surroundings we use. It is worth reading because it reframes where thinking actually takes place, and suggests that leaning on external carriers can sharpen focus, understanding, and creativity at once.

articles.failureAnalysis: 这类 Awesome/综述仓库的天花板通常很低：它聚合链接，却难以提供可复现的基准、数据或成本对比，读者看完仍不知道哪个方法在真实业务里更划算。多个关键词（循环工程、Harness 工程等）尚未形成行业共识，很可能只是把一个普通概念重新包装，热度过去后词条即被弃用。324 星属于小众规模，更新与维护高度依赖少数作者，容易出现链接失效、内容停滞。缺少真实部署案例与失败复盘，使它在实际选型时说服力有限。

zh.title: 图工程全景综述：从本体工程到提示工程的六层工程栈
zh.highlight: 仓库以一张综述地图把本体工程、图工程、循环工程、Harness 工程、上下文工程与提示工程并列在一起。
zh.summary: 这是一个获得约 324 星、近期仍有公开活动的 GitHub 仓库，定位于汇总“本体工程、图工程、循环工程、Harness 工程、上下文工程与提示工程”方向的综述材料。它值得关注的地方在于：试图把当前 AI 应用里散落的几个热门概念放进同一个知识框架，方便非技术读者快速建立概念坐标系。
zh.failureAnalysis: 这类 Awesome/综述仓库的天花板通常很低：它聚合链接，却难以提供可复现的基准、数据或成本对比，读者看完仍不知道哪个方法在真实业务里更划算。多个关键词（循环工程、Harness 工程等）尚未形成行业共识，很可能只是把一个普通概念重新包装，热度过去后词条即被弃用。324 星属于小众规模，更新与维护高度依赖少数作者，容易出现链接失效、内容停滞。缺少真实部署案例与失败复盘，使它在实际选型时说服力有限。

en.highlight: The repository's description lines up ontology engineering, graph engineering, loop engineering, harness engineering, context engineering and prompt engineering in one survey map.
en.summary: This is a GitHub repository with roughly 324 stars and recent public activity, positioning itself as a collection of survey material across ontology, graph, loop, harness, context and prompt engineering. It is worth a look because it tries to place several scattered AI-application buzzwords into a single conceptual framework for non-technical readers.
en.failureAnalysis: Awesome-list style surveys rarely offer reproducible benchmarks, data or cost comparisons, so they cannot tell you which method actually pays off in production; the self-coined terms may fade once the hype passes, and maintenance depends on a small group of authors.
en.title: Awesome Graph Engineering: A Six-Layer Survey from Ontology to Prompt Engineering

articles.title: AI Engineer Notebooks – free, framework-free RAG/agents/evals on Colab
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: GitHub + HN discussion
articles.summary: 这是一个 GitHub 项目，提供一批可直接在 Colab 运行的笔记本，用最少的框架依赖演示 RAG、智能体（agents）与评估（evals）三类 AI 应用核心环节。它值得关注的点在于：把常被框架封装起来的流程拆到笔记本里，让工程师能看清每一步到底发生了什么，同时零成本上手。
articles.failureAnalysis: 第一，免框架的教学价值与工程落地之间存在落差：真实业务需要重试、监控、并发与成本控制，笔记本很难覆盖，用户看完仍要自己搭一套。第二，同类开源教程和官方文档极多，免费内容缺乏清晰的变现与维护动力，作者一旦停更就会迅速过时。第三，Colab 免费额度有限、依赖版本易变，示例跑不通会直接劝退，而 AI 生态迭代快，维护成本持续上升。
articles.highlight: 免费、不依赖框架的 RAG、智能体与评估（evals）笔记本，可直接在 Colab 上运行。

en.highlight: Free, framework-free notebooks for RAG, agents, and evals that run directly on Colab.
en.summary: This is a GitHub project offering Colab-ready notebooks that demonstrate the core parts of RAG, agents, and evaluation with minimal framework dependencies. It is worth reading because it strips away framework abstraction so engineers can see each step of the pipeline, at zero setup cost.
en.failureAnalysis: Notebooks teach the concepts but do not cover the retries, monitoring, concurrency, and cost control that real deployments require. Free tutorial content also faces heavy competition and weak maintenance incentives, so examples can rot quickly as Colab limits and library versions change.
